exposure: Two-step labor induction (vaginal prostaglandins followed by prostaglandins or oxytocin)
Two-step labor induction by vaginal prostaglandins followed by a second cycle of prostaglandins or intravenous oxytocin
outcome: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean section)
cohort: 157 women who underwent a two-step labor induction
finding: While two-step labor induction had a fairly good success rate, advanced maternal age and nulliparity were associated with higher Cesarean section rates, whereas Group B streptococcus colonization and favorable cervical status after the first induction were associated with higher vaginal delivery rates.
mod_finding: Labor induction with two cycles of pharmacological stimulation had a fairly good success rate and a low risk of complications, with factors predicting vaginal delivery including younger maternal age, parity, positive group B streptococcus colonization, and favorable cervical status after the first stimulation cycle.
